articles.title: In 2008, 50 Cent helped transform a neglected Queens garden with a rainwater harvesting system; 18 years later, the community green space still carries his name
articles.summary: Nearly two decades ago, rapper 50 Cent (Curtis James Jackson) joined an effort to transform an underused community garden in Queens into a public green
articles.body: Nearly two decades ago, rapper 50 Cent (Curtis James Jackson) joined an effort to transform an underused community garden in Queens into a public green space designed for gardening, recreation and community gatherings. Today, the site continues to carry his name as the Curtis “50 Cent” Jackson Community Garden.The project began in 2007 and had a personal significance for Jackson, who grew up in Queens and wanted to contribute to the neighborhood. He partnered with New York Restoration Project (NYRP) founder and performer Bette Midler as part of the initiative to restore the neglected space.Financial support for the garden’s transformation came from Jackson’s G-Unity Foundation. Following the redevelopment, the property officially reopened in November 2008.The redesigned space was created with landscape architect and designer Walter Hood, whose work gave the garden a broader purpose beyond traditional gardening. The site was envisioned as a place where residents could grow plants, spend time outdoors and come together as a community. The redevelopment also introduced features intended to make the space more useful for both gardeners and visitors.The rainwater system became a defining featureOne of the most notable elements of the garden is its rainwater collection system. Large funnels measuring 10 feet in height were installed to capture rainwater, which could then be used to irrigate the garden.The structures were designed to serve more than one function. Along with collecting water, the tall funnels provide shade, creating areas where visitors can sit, relax and take a break. The system therefore combined an environmental function with a practical feature for people using the garden.Why the garden matters to Jamaica, QueensThe garden is located in Jamaica, a Queens neighborhood where access to open space has been a longstanding concern. The area has less than five percent of the recommended amount of open space for its population of more than tens of thousands of children.That makes community spaces such as the Curtis “50 Cent” Jackson Community Garden particularly significant. The property provides an outdoor setting that brings together gardening, recreation and opportunities for residents to gather.Further upgrades came in 2020The garden received another round of improvements in 2020, with Walter Hood and the Knight Foundation supporting the work.Among the additions was a solar-powered water pump, along with newly built garden beds. The upgrades continued the site’s development as a functioning community garden and public outdoor space.Who is 50 Cent?Curtis Jackson, professionally known as 50 Cent, is a rapper, actor and entrepreneur who rose to prominence in hip-hop before expanding his career into television, film and business.As a recording artist, he became one of the prominent names in rap and subsequently built a career across multiple areas of entertainment. His work has included music, acting, television projects and entrepreneurial ventures. Jackson has also participated in philanthropic and community-focused initiatives, including the Queens garden project supported through his G-Unity Foundation.From Baisley Park Community Garden to the Curtis Jackson Community GardenWhat began as an effort to restore a neglected garden in Queens ultimately created a long-term public green space. The former Baisley Park Community Garden was transformed through a collaboration involving 50 Cent, his G-Unity Foundation, Bette Midler and NYRP, with Walter Hood contributing the landscape design.The garden reopened in November 2008 with features including 10-foot rainwater-collecting funnels that also provide shade. Further work in 2020 brought a solar-powered water pump and additional garden beds.Eighteen years after its reopening, the Curtis “50 Cent” Jackson Community Garden continues to stand as a community-oriented green space in Jamaica, Queens.Around 1996, 50 Cent entered the underground rap scene in Queens, which is where he first started his career in music. Initially, he connected with Jam Master Jay of Run-D.M.C., who trained him and helped him structure songs. Finally, in 1999, he landed a record deal and finally started working on his debut album, ‘Power of the Dollar’.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Quote of the day by Diane Keaton: ‘You can't hold on to happiness or a good moment, but it will be back. And the memory will stay,’ a powerful life lesson that highlights the importance of embracing every moment
articles.summary: Diane Keaton reflects on the fleeting nature of happiness and the power of memories in her quote, reminding us to appreciate the good moments in life as they come and to cherish the memories they leave behind.
articles.body: Some of the best things in life are also the hardest to keep. A great day ends, people move on, relationships change, and even the happiest moments eventually become memories. Diane Keaton had a rather simple way of looking at that.Today’s quote of the day by Diane Keaton reads: “You can't hold on to happiness or a good moment, but it will be back. And the memory will stay.”In a 1987 interview with Vanity Fair, Keaton spoke about happiness while discussing her film 'Crimes of the Heart', her ideas about life and the way good moments come and go. She recalled the ending of the play and film, where happiness is treated as something that exists only for a moment rather than something we can hold on to forever.What does the quote by Diane Keaton mean?Diane Keaton’s quote is not really saying that happiness disappears for good. It is more about accepting that a happy moment has a natural ending. That can be difficult to accept. When something is going really well, there is often a temptation to hold on to it. We want the holiday to last longer, the relationship to stay the same, the exciting new job to always feel exciting or a particular period of our lives to never change.But life does not really work that way. Keaton’s point is that a good moment ending does not make it meaningless. You experienced it. You got to have it. And later, the memory of it can become its own kind of comfort.There is also something hopeful in the second half of the quote. She says the good moment “will be back.” It might not return in the same form, and it might not happen when we expect it to, but another good moment can come along.How is the quote by Diane Keaton relevant today?It is easy to feel like life has to be perfect all the time, especially now when people are constantly seeing other people's happiest moments online. A vacation ends. A friendship changes. College comes to an end. People leave jobs. Even periods when everything seems to be going right eventually shift into something else.Keaton’s quote offers a different way of looking at that change. Instead of thinking that a good period is ruined because it ended, there is room to simply be grateful that it happened.The memory matters too. Sometimes years later, a song, photograph, old message or even a random smell can take someone straight back to a particular time in their life. The moment is gone, but the feeling attached to it can still exist.That idea was particularly relevant to Keaton when she spoke to Vanity Fair in 1987. She said that people have things in their lives that are wonderful but do not last very long, and later described the ending of 'Crimes of the Heart' as capturing the idea that happiness is only there “for a moment.”Early life of Diane KeatonDiane Keaton was born Diane Hall on January 5, 1946, in Los Angeles. She grew up in Santa Ana, California, as the oldest of four children. Her father was a civil engineer who later became a real estate broker, while her mother was an artist.Keaton developed an interest in performing when she was young. She took part in school productions and talent shows before eventually leaving California for New York at 19 to study acting at the Neighborhood Playhouse.She soon began working in theatre. In 1968, Keaton joined the original Broadway production of 'Hair'. She later appeared opposite Woody Allen in the Broadway production of 'Play It Again, Sam,' which became an important turning point in her career. Her career was not simply built around comedy, either. Keaton moved between theatre, comedy and serious dramatic roles, something that became a recurring part of her work.How did Diane Keaton rise to fame?Keaton became widely known through her work with Woody Allen, particularly after appearing in films including 'Sleeper' and 'Love and Death'. But it was 'Annie Hall' in 1977 that changed the scale of her career.Keaton played the title character, a role that became closely associated with her personality and distinctive fashion sense. The film became a major success, and Keaton won the Academy Award for Best Actress at the 1978 Oscars. 'Annie Hall' also won Best Picture that year.She continued to take on very different roles, including Kay Adams in 'The Godfather' films and Louise Bryant in 'Reds'. In 1986, she starred alongside Jessica Lange and Sissy Spacek in 'Crimes of the Heart,' playing Lenny MaGrath, one of three sisters dealing with complicated family relationships and personal struggles. Vanity Fair's 1987 profile noted how different the role was from some of her earlier performances.By the time Keaton spoke to Vanity Fair in 1987, she had already experienced the highs and pressures of fame. But her comments about happiness were surprisingly uncomplicated.You cannot make a good moment stay forever. You can enjoy it while it is there. You can remember it when it is gone. And, eventually, another one might come along. That may be the simplest part of Diane Keaton's philosophy, and perhaps the reason this quote still feels so relatable.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: 'Backrooms' starts streaming this week: Here are 6 eerie films to check out beyond Kane Parsons' record-breaking A24 movie
articles.summary: Ready to step into the world of liminal space horror? We have some recommendations for you.
articles.body:
Our experts independently review everything we recommend. If you buy through our links, we may earn commission.

Backrooms left audiences stuck in the loop, craving more liminal horror. This week, Kane Parsons' record-breaking A24 directorial debut starts streaming on HBO Max , so you'll be able to revisit those creepy yellow halls as often as you'd like. Starring Chiwetel Ejiofor and Renate Reinsve, Backrooms is about one of the internet's favorite urban legends, and it expands upon Parsons' own web series exploring the creepypasta phenomenon .

Here's where and when you can stream Backrooms, plus a few more recommendations for liminal and psychological horror films.

When does Backrooms come out on streaming?

Backrooms starts streaming Sept. 25 on HBO Max.

Kane Parsons' original found-footage short-film series, which inspired the 2026 movie, is available to watch for free on YouTube.

While Backrooms premieres on HBO Max on Sept. 25, it's unclear whether the extended director's cut, Backrooms: Everything Must Go Edition, will also be available to stream.

While Kane Parsons' A24 blockbuster introduced many viewers to liminal-space horror, it's not the only film that explores the terror of the infinite (or the creepiest corners of the internet). Here are a few more movies to check out if you liked Backrooms:

Neon's It Ends was released in the shadow of Backrooms , so while the two films share producers, you may have missed this quieter liminal horror movie about a group of friends who wind up on a seemingly endless roadtrip. Phinehas Yoon, Akira Jackson, Noah Toth and Mitchell Cole star. It's available to rent or buy on Apple TV , Amazon Prime Video and other video-on-demand platforms.

In an attempt to exit a subway station, a man becomes lost inside a loop of tunnels filled with horrifying anomalies, and must follow increasingly confusing directions to reach Exit 8. Kazunari Ninomiya stars in this psychological horror film, currently available to stream on AMC+ .

We're All Going to the World's Fair (2021)

For anyone who got the chance to see Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma this summer, consider checking out Jane Schoenbrun's feature directorial debut. We're All Going to the World's Fair follows a lonely teenager participating in an online challenge that promises to cause mental and physical changes. The psychological horror-drama uses the found footage style to explore a particularly unsettling corner of the internet. Anna Cobb stars in the film, which you can stream on Mubi .

Jesse Eisenberg and Imogen Poots star as a young couple who, upon visiting a housing development, become trapped within a neighborhood of identical looking units. This sci-fi thriller streams free with ads on Tubi.

Liminal space, but make it aliens. This star-studded sci-fi horror film follows a biologist who joins an expedition into Area X to find out what happened to her husband. The cast includes Natalie Portman, Jennifer Jason Leigh, Gina Rodriguez, Tessa Thompson and Oscar Isaac. You can watch Annihilation with MGM+ .

If you really want more creepy, endless hallways and no way out, well, "Heeeere's Johnny!" Stanley Kubrick's 1980 psychological horror film follows a family of winter caretakers for the Overlook Hotel. Jack Nicholson, Shelley Duvall and Danny Lloyd star in this classic, which is available to stream on Philo .

articles.title: Renner lamenta morte de Rick em vídeo após acidente de helicóptero | G1
articles.standfirst: Cantor sertanejo morreu em acidente de helicóptero na terça-feira (22). Dupla se apresentou junta por cerca de 40 anos.
articles.summary: Em vídeo emocionante, Renner lamenta a morte de Rick após 40 anos de dupla e agradece o apoio dos fãs depois de trágico acidente de helicóptero.
articles.body:
Renner lamentou a morte do parceiro de dupla sertaneja, Rick , em vídeo publicado nesta quinta-feira (24). O cantor morreu em acidente de helicóptero, com outras quatro pessoas, nesta terça (22).

"Eu resolvi aparecer agora somente porque a gente passou por momentos bem difíceis até agora. Porque só a gente que está na pele, próximos assim, sente, né? Afinal de contas, foram 40 anos de vivência, de muito suor, muita luta. Então, não é fácil. Mas Deus está dando a força. A gente vai aos poucos vai levantar, né?", afirmou Renner, na primeira manifestação que fez sobre a morte.

"A saudade vai ficar, mas eu estou passando aqui para agradecer aos milhões de mensagens carinhosas para comigo e para com as famílias, né? Todas as famílias que estavam envolvidas também nesse dia, de uma certa forma, né? Então, obrigado, Brasil. Obrigado, mundo. Vocês são maravilhosos. Esse carinho que eu sempre digo não tem preço. É o que levanta a gente, o que conforta, tá?"

A dupla sertaneja Rick & Renner foi formada nos anos 1980, em Brasília, e começou a fazer sucesso nos anos 1990, antes da explosão do chamado sertanejo universitário, que renovou o estilo. Entre os principais sucessos da dupla estão "Ela é demais" (do refrão "uma deusa, uma louca, uma feiticeira") e "Nos bares da cidade" .

Rick e Renner durante apresentação no Vila Country, em São Paulo. — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram/RickeRenner

Os destroços do helicóptero com Rick, foram encontrados na região de Santa Bárbara, no interior de Urubici, após desaparecer na segunda (21). Cinco corpos foram localizados, de acordo com o Corpo de Bombeiros.

Além do cantor, estavam na aeronave o empresário Bruno Avelar, o videomaker Paulo Soares, o piloto Antônio Roberto Nóbrega de Araújo e o copiloto Leopoldo Barros Teixeira.

"Eu passei aqui pra dizer que amo vocês, que o show não pode parar, não é? A gente vai continuar cantando. E é isso. Obrigado. Se eu puder resumir tudo isso, eu vou falar assim pra vocês: gratidão, tá? Muito obrigado a todos vocês", afirmou Renner.

"Estou bem, tá? Estou bem, estou forte no Senhor Jesus, tá? Você que está assistindo a esse vídeo, seja forte também no seu Jesus, tá bom? Ele ama você e vai te dar estratégias e o suporte necessário espiritual pra você, bem direto do Reino, tá bom? Um beijo a todos os fãs do Rick & Renner do Brasil e do mundo, e até breve, tá? Muito obrigado. Beijo."

24ª FECOIMP reuniu negócios, conhecimento e
experiências para diferentes públicos | G1
articles.standfirst: Em quatro dias de programação, feira reuniu empresas, capacitação, gastronomia, cultura e iniciativas de inclusão no Centro de Convenções de Imperatriz.
articles.summary:
Em quatro dias de programação, feira reuniu empresas, capacitação, gastronomia,
cultura e iniciativas de inclusão no Centro de Convenções de Imperatriz.
articles.body:
Quatro dias de encontros empresariais, conhecimento, gastronomia, cultura e novas experiências marcaram a 24a edição da Feira do Comércio, Indústria e Serviços de Imperatriz (FECOIMP). Realizado de 16 a 19 de setembro, no Centro de Convenções de Imperatriz, o evento encerrou mais uma edição reforçando uma proposta que vai além da exposição de marcas, produtos e serviços.

Sob o tema “Aqui vira negócio”, a FECOIMP 2026 reuniu diferentes setores e públicos em uma programação construída para estimular relacionamento, geração de oportunidades, qualificação profissional e experiências dentro do ambiente da feira.

Além dos estandes, a edição contou com iniciativas voltadas diretamente à aproximação entre empresas, espaços de capacitação, programação gastronômica e cultural e ações inéditas de inclusão.

O ambiente de negócios esteve presente em diferentes momentos da programação. A Rodada de Negócios ACII/Sebrae e o Encontro de Negócios PDF Maranhão/FIEMA criaram espaços direcionados à aproximação entre fornecedores e potenciais compradores.

As iniciativas permitiram que empresas apresentassem produtos, serviços e capacidade de atendimento, conhecessem demandas de mercado e ampliassem possibilidades de relacionamento comercial.

A dinâmica complementou o contato realizado diariamente entre expositores e visitantes, ampliando as formas de interação empresarial dentro da FECOIMP.

A programação também abriu espaço para capacitação profissional. Por meio do ACII Capacita, empresários, profissionais e estudantes tiveram acesso a conteúdos relacionados a áreas estratégicas do ambiente empresarial, como marketing, vendas, inovação, tecnologia, gestão e liderança.

A proposta foi aproximar conhecimento e prática, inserindo a qualificação profissional dentro da própria experiência da feira.

A gastronomia também esteve presente com o 6o Festival Gastronômico da FECOIMP, que mobilizou estabelecimentos e público desde a etapa de votação popular até a final realizada no último dia do evento.

A programação cultural completou a agenda, levando diferentes atrações aos espaços da feira durante os quatro dias.

Novidades ampliaram os públicos da FECOIMP

A edição de 2026 também foi marcada pela implantação de novas iniciativas.

Pela primeira vez na história da FECOIMP, o evento contou com uma Sala Sensorial integrada ao Espaço de Inclusão. O ambiente foi planejado para oferecer acolhimento, conforto e regulação sensorial a pessoas que pudessem apresentar sobrecarga diante dos diferentes estímulos de um evento de grande porte.

Estruturada com atenção especial às pessoas com Transtorno do Espectro Autista (TEA), pessoas com deficiência, pessoas com outros transtornos do neurodesenvolvimento e visitantes com hipersensibilidade ou sobrecarga sensorial, a iniciativa ampliou as condições de participação de diferentes públicos na feira.

Outra novidade foi o Fecoimp Kids, iniciativa direcionada a crianças de 8 a 12 anos, que aproximou o público infantil do ambiente da FECOIMP por meio de atividades e experiências relacionadas ao empreendedorismo.

Uma edição construída por diferentes frentes

A combinação de negócios, conhecimento, gastronomia, cultura e inclusão ajudou a compor a experiência da FECOIMP 2026 e a ampliar as possibilidades de participação durante os quatro dias de evento.

Realizada pela Associação Comercial, Industrial e Serviços de Imperatriz (ACII), a FECOIMP encerra sua 24a edição mantendo sua trajetória como um ambiente de encontro entre empresas, instituições, profissionais e sociedade.

Mais do que concentrar diferentes setores em um mesmo espaço, a edição de 2026 deixa como registro a ampliação das experiências oferecidas ao público e a incorporação de iniciativas que podem contribuir para a evolução das próximas edições.

articles.title: Eneida Agra Maracajá recebe título de Doutora Honoris Causa da UEPB | G1
articles.standfirst: Professora e ativista cultural, Eneida é idealizadora do Festival de Inverno de Campina Grande, que completou 51 anos em 2026.
articles.summary: Eneida Agra Maracajá, idealizadora do Festival de Inverno de Campina Grande, recebe o título de Doutora Honoris Causa da UEPB por sua contribuição histórica à cultura.
articles.body:
UEPB aprova título de Doutora Honoris Causa para Eneida Agra Maracajá — Foto: Yago Paolo/G1 PB

A professora e ativista cultural de Campina Grande Eneida Agra Maracajá foi escolhida para receber o título de Doutora Honoris Causa da Universidade Estadual da Paraíba (UEPB). A homenagem foi aprovada por unanimidade pelo Conselho Universitário (Consuni) da instituição, durante reunião realizada nesta quarta-feira (23).

O título é uma das maiores honrarias concedidas pela universidade e é destinado a personalidades que tenham se destacado pelo saber ou pela atuação nas artes, ciências, filosofia, letras ou pelo entendimento entre os povos. Durante a reunião, conselheiros destacaram a atuação de Eneida na cultura e nas artes, especialmente na Rainha da Borborema.

Eneida Agra Maracajá é idealizadora do Festival de Inverno de Campina Grande (FICG), criado na década de 1970 e que completou 51 anos em 2026.

O festival surgiu a partir de um evento dedicado ao teatro, o Festival Nacional de Teatro (FENAT), realizado em 1974. Depois, passou a reunir diferentes manifestações artísticas, como teatro, dança, música, artes plásticas e literatura.

Em 2019, em entrevista ao g1 , Eneida relembrou a criação do festival e contou que, nos primeiros anos, artistas de diferentes estados chegaram a Campina Grande para participar das atividades. Segundo ela, o evento começou com apoio de recursos federais, estaduais e municipais, além de doações de moradores da cidade.

Além do FICG, Eneida criou projetos culturais voltados à população, como o Cultura no Presídio, realizado durante 13 anos no Complexo Penitenciário do Serrotão, e o Tamanquinhos das Artes, desenvolvido com crianças em situação de vulnerabilidade social.

Ela também foi diretora do Teatro Municipal Severino Cabral em duas gestões e secretária de Cultura de Campina Grande entre 2011 e 2012.

Eneida é graduada em Pedagogia e tem mestrado em Educação. É professora efetiva da Universidade Federal da Paraíba (UFPB) e teve passagem pela própria UEPB e pela Faculdade Católica de Filosofia de Campina Grande.

Eneida Agra Maracajá é idealizadora do Festival de Inverno de Campina Grande (FICG), criado na década de 1970 e que completou 51 anos em 2026. — Foto: Divulgação/FICG

Durante a reunião que aprovou o título, a reitora Célia Regina afirmou que a homenagem reconhece a trajetória de Eneida e sua atuação em defesa da cultura.

A vice-reitora Ivonildes Fonseca, o pró-reitor de Cultura da UEPB, José Cristóvão de Andrade, e outros integrantes do Consuni também destacaram a contribuição da professora para as artes e a cultura.

A universidade ainda deverá definir a data e os procedimentos para a entrega do título de Doutora Honoris Causa.

articles.title: Festival de Bandas e Fanfarras do Lago Grande ocorre em Curuai | G1
articles.standfirst: Evento reúne estudantes de Santarém e Juruti em apresentações musicais e coreográficas no Lago Grande
articles.summary: O Festival de Bandas e Fanfarras do Lago Grande reúne estudantes de Santarém e Juruti em Vila Curuai com apresentações musicais nesta sexta-feira.
articles.body:
Festival de Bandas e Fanfarras do Lago Grande reúne estudantes nesta sexta. — Foto: Agência Santarém

O distrito de Vila Curuai, na região do Lago Grande, em Santarém , recebe nesta sexta-feira (25), a partir das 19h, o III Festival de Bandas e Fanfarras do Lago Grande. O evento reúne estudantes, regentes, famílias e comunidades em uma programação que celebra a música, a cultura escolar e o talento de jovens da região.

Realizado pela Prefeitura de Santarém, por meio da Secretaria Municipal de Educação (Semed), em parceria com a Agência Distrital de Vila Curuai, o festival chega à terceira edição com quatro categorias de apresentação, reunindo bandas de diferentes níveis e formações.

Entre os destaques estão as Bandas de Percussão Iniciante, que contam com a participação de escolas do Lago Grande e também do município de Juruti.

Além de valorizar as apresentações musicais e coreográficas, o festival busca estimular entre os estudantes valores como disciplina, convivência, trabalho em equipe e participação comunitária. A programação também promove a integração entre as comunidades e fortalece a tradição das bandas e fanfarras como instrumentos de educação e cultura.

Cada grupo terá até 13 minutos para realizar sua apresentação. Desse tempo, até cinco minutos serão destinados ao deslocamento e até oito minutos à execução musical e coreográfica.

articles.title: Exposição de Marcone Moreira apresenta Amazônia contemporânea e em transformação em São Luís | G1
articles.standfirst: Com curadoria de Eucanaã Ferraz, mostra “O mundo em trânsito de Marcone Moreira” reúne obras que dialogam com paisagem, memória e deslocamentos.
articles.summary: Com curadoria de Eucanaã Ferraz, mostra “O mundo em trânsito de Marcone Moreira” reúne obras que dialogam com paisagem, memória e deslocamentos.
articles.body:
Exposição de Marcone Moreira apresenta uma Amazônia contemporânea e em transformação em São Luís — Foto: Divulgação/Assessoria

O CHÃO SLZ, em São Luís , recebe entre os dias 7 de outubro e 7 de novembro de 2026 a exposição “O mundo em trânsito de Marcone Moreira”, com curadoria do poeta e pesquisador Eucanaã Ferraz. A mostra reúne trabalhos de diferentes fases da trajetória do artista paraense e propõe uma reflexão sobre a Amazônia como território de memória, transformação e criação.

A abertura será realizada no dia 7 de outubro, às 18h30, com a presença de Marcone Moreira. A entrada é gratuita.O evento inclui uma visita à exposição e uma conversa entre o artista e Dinho Araújo sobre os processos criativos, materiais e referências que atravessam sua produção.

Nascido em Pio XII (MA) e radicado no Pará, Marcone Moreira desenvolve sua pesquisa a partir das paisagens e experiências de Marabá (PA), cidade marcada pela presença dos rios Tocantins e Itacaiúnas. Sua obra transforma materiais do cotidiano, como madeiras, peças de embarcações e elementos ligados ao trabalho popular, em construções visuais que aproximam passado e presente.

Segundo Eucanaã Ferraz, a exposição parte da ideia de um “mundo em trânsito”, no qual diferentes tempos, materiais e sentidos estão em permanente transformação. A mostra apresenta a Amazônia não como um cenário distante ou exótico, mas como um espaço simbólico atravessado por histórias, conflitos, deslocamentos e reinvenções.

Obras revelam relações entre paisagem e memória

A exposição reúne séries importantes da carreira do artista, como “Cruzamentos”, formada por composições feitas com madeiras e parafusos retirados de carrocerias de caminhões. Os trabalhos remetem aos caminhos percorridos entre rios e estradas, além das relações entre presença e ausência.

Nas séries “Páginas” e “Rotas”, Marcone utiliza madeiras de embarcações desgastadas pelo tempo para criar composições cromáticas que aproximam referências do construtivismo brasileiro do imaginário popular amazônico.

Já as pinturas da série “Travessias” apresentam figuras solitárias em embarcações, criando imagens associadas aos percursos humanos entre trabalho, memória, mito e território.

Entre as instalações está “Vertebral”, uma escultura formada por hélices de alumínio organizadas em movimento sinuoso, em referência à força da sucuri, símbolo presente no imaginário amazônico. A mostra também apresenta “Exaustos”, instalação composta por porretes e cepos de madeira utilizados no processamento do babaçu e da castanha-do-pará.

Artista transforma materiais cotidianos em linguagem poética

A produção de Marcone Moreira combina pintura, escultura, vídeo, fotografia e instalação, tendo como eixo a investigação sobre memória e deslocamento simbólico dos materiais. Desde o final dos anos 1990, o artista participa de exposições no Brasil e no exterior.

Entre suas principais mostras individuais estão “Território líquido” (Instituto Tomie Ohtake, 2015), “Marcone Moreira” (Paço Imperial, 2016), “Linhas de Força” (Palácio das Artes, 2017), “Exaustos” (Casa das Onze Janelas, 2018), “Conjunção” (Gomide, 2020), “Fraturas” (Portas Vilaseca Galeria, 2024) e “Entre Ruínas: o mundo em trânsito” (CAIXA Cultural São Paulo, 2025).

O artista também participou de exposições coletivas como o Panorama da Arte Brasileira (MAM-SP, 2003), “Os Trópicos” (Martin-Gropius-Bau, Berlim, 2008), “From the Margin to the Edge” (Somerset House, Londres, 2012), “VAIVÉM” (CCBB, 2019) e a 6ª Bienal de Montevidéu (2025).

Ao longo da carreira, recebeu prêmios e bolsas, entre eles o Bolsa Pampulha, do Museu de Arte da Pampulha, o Prêmio Marcantonio Vilaça, a Bolsa de Pesquisa Funarte e o Prêmio PREAMAR de Arte e Cultura.

Eucanaã Ferraz nasceu no Rio de Janeiro, em 1961. É poeta, professor de Literatura Brasileira na Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro (UFRJ) e consultor de Literatura do Instituto Moreira Salles desde 2010.

Como curador, realizou exposições dedicadas a artistas como Fayga Ostrower, Raul Mourão, Vicente de Mello, José Bechara e Chichico Alkmim. Também foi responsável, ao lado de Veronica Stigger, pela exposição “Constelação Clarice” (IMS, 2018–2022), reconhecida pela revista Frieze entre as dez melhores mostras do mundo em 2022.

Sua atuação reúne literatura, artes visuais e música, com pesquisas voltadas às diferentes formas de criação artística.

articles.title: Sandy & Junior sinalizam volta da dupla em 2027 – ação de retorno (financeiro) garantido na era dos megashows | G1
articles.body:
Sandy e Junior durante show da turnê 'Nossa História' em São Paulo (SP), em 2019 — Foto: Fábio Tito / g1

♬ Sandy & Junior sinalizam outra volta aos palcos em 2027, oito anos após o primeiro retorno dessa dupla que arrastou multidões pelo Brasil ao longo de 2019 com a turnê do show “Nossa história”.

Por ora, há apenas um anúncio enigmático nas redes sociais em que está escrito “S&J – São Paulo – 2027”. Maiores detalhes serão revelados somente em novembro.

Nada foi revelado de concreto, mas bastou criar o mistério para que a ação de marketing surtisse imediato efeito nos milhões de saudosos fãs da dupla formada em 1989 – quando Sandy Leah e Junior Lima ainda eram crianças – e dissolvida amigavelmente em 2007.

Ou seja, fará 20 anos da separação da dupla em 2027, ocasião propícia para mais uma volta à cena dos irmãos paulistas. Esse retorno seria perfeitamente natural na era dos megashows produzidos por grandes empresas com patrocínio de marcas milionárias. Nesse contexto, um retorno de Sandy & Junior é uma ação certeira.

Afinal, se Xuxa – símbolo da nostalgia infantil dos anos 1980 – voltou à cena neste ano de 2026 em turnê concorrida em estádios e arenas, o caminho natural e até óbvio seria promover em 2027 a volta de Sandy & Junior, dupla que marcou gerações de crianças e adolescentes ao longo da década de 1990 e dos anos 2000.

articles.title: 'I have never met late Disha Salian or Aditya Thackeray ever in my life': Sooraj Pancholi issues fresh statement after CBI probe, urges agencies to investigate ‘thoroughly and completely’
articles.summary: Actor Sooraj Pancholi has once again addressed the controversy surrounding his name in the Disha Salian death case, saying he has spent years being linked
articles.body: Actor Sooraj Pancholi has once again addressed the controversy surrounding his name in the Disha Salian death case, saying he has spent years being linked to a matter with which he maintains he has no connection. In a lengthy statement shared on social media, Pancholi denied ever meeting Disha Salian or Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Aaditya Thackeray and said he remains willing to cooperate with the ongoing investigation.The actor also alleged that the online scrutiny surrounding the case had escalated into abuse and death threats. He said he wanted a transparent investigation and asked the authorities to make his exoneration equally clear if the probe finds no evidence connecting him to the case.Sooraj Pancholi says he has ‘nothing to hide’In his latest statement on his social media handle, Pancholi said he had never met Disha Salian or Aaditya Thackeray, either directly or indirectly.“I Have never met late Disha Salian or Aditya Thackeray ever in my life. Not directly. Not indirectly!” he wrote.Pancholi said his name had been repeatedly dragged into the matter over the years despite his denial of any connection to Salian or the circumstances surrounding her death. He added that the renewed attention came at a time when he was attempting to rebuild his career and personal life.“And now, when I am finally trying to rebuild my life, my career and my future, I refuse to stay silent and watch it happen all over again,” he wrote, adding that he had “nothing to hide or run away from”.The actor also said he was not seeking sympathy or asking people to take his side, but was instead calling for transparency and a fair investigation.Sooraj Pancholi says he is ready to face any investigationPancholi reiterated that he had cooperated with authorities and remained prepared to answer questions as the CBI investigation progresses.“I have cooperated. I have answered questions. I have made myself available. I have said clearly that I am ready to face any investigation,” he said.He further stated that if investigators found evidence connecting him to the case, he would accept whatever punishment was determined under the law.“If there is even one small piece of evidence or any involvement connecting me to this matter, I am willing to face whatever punishment the law decides, without any questions,” Pancholi wrote.At the same time, he appealed to the investigating agencies and sections of the media to state clearly if the investigation establishes that he had no involvement.“But if the investigation by the investigating agencies establishes that I genuinely have nothing to do with it, then I request the investigating agencies and the so called ‘HONEST MEDIA’ to please say that loud and clearly,” he wrote.Sooraj Pancholi alleges online abuse and death threatsPancholi also spoke about the impact of the repeated allegations and online commentary surrounding his name. He alleged that the situation had gone beyond criticism and said he had received death threats.He criticised what he described as the manner in which sections of the media have covered the case, arguing that every report and allegation has consequences for the people involved.“This may be entertainment or a dinner time story for some people, but this is my life!” he wrote.Pancholi also alleged that some of the attempts to associate his name with the case were connected to issues involving members of his family. He said he had no personal issues with anyone and maintained that he had no political alliances or agenda.Sooraj Pancholi wants to speak at length about the caseThe actor said his latest statement did not contain everything he wanted to say. He explained that he wanted to publish it before his Instagram account was blocked, a development he said he did not understand. Pancholi added that he wanted an opportunity to speak to a journalist or interviewer who would ask him difficult and uncomfortable questions directly.“There is a lot I want to say. There are things I have stayed quiet about for years,” he wrote. “When I finally get the right opportunity, I will answer them. Every question. Directly. Honestly. Without fear.”He also said he wanted such a conversation to focus on facts rather than sensationalism.“When I speak, I want to speak properly with nothing held back and with the truth being given the space it deserves,” Pancholi added.What happened in the Disha Salian death case?Disha Salian, who had worked as a manager for late actor Sushant Singh Rajput, died on June 8, 2020, after falling from a building in Mumbai’s Malad area. The Mumbai Police initially registered an accidental death report, and subsequent investigations had not established foul play. The case was later revisited following a petition by Salian’s father, Satish Salian.On September 2, 2026, the Bombay High Court directed the CBI to investigate the circumstances surrounding Salian’s death and ordered the agency to register an FIR and record her father’s statement. The court also made an important distinction regarding the status of people whose names had surfaced in allegations, stating that no individual should be treated as an accused unless sufficient material emerged during the investigation.The CBI subsequently registered an FIR on September 13. The FIR invoked provisions concerning criminal conspiracy, gang rape, murder, disappearance of evidence and alleged misconduct by public servants, but did not name any individual as an accused. Reports said the roles of several people were to be investigated as part of the probe.Aaditya Thackeray also denies knowing Disha SalianAaditya Thackeray has separately denied ever meeting or knowing Salian. Following the CBI FIR, he described attempts to link him to the case as an “evidence-free” campaign and called the allegations an attempt at character assassination.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. That was September 27th, 2013. Now September 27th, 2014, he marries Amal. Now that’s good karma right there," Gerber said. Shortly after the Clooneys welcomed their twins in 2017, George and Rande sold their Casamigos tequila brand for $1 billion to British beverage giant Diageo. Dolph Lundgren was preparing to die. The Swedish actor, who famously played Soviet boxer Ivan Drago in "Rocky IV," has written a new memoir, "Fights Worth Fighting: Finding Strength in Struggle." In it, the 68-year-old details his grueling journey with cancer. ‘ROCKY’ STAR DOLPH LUNDGREN SWEARS BY THIS SECRET FOR STRONG MARRIAGE Fox News may be compensated for or earn a commission if you buy through our referral links. The star was diagnosed in 2015 after doctors found a cancerous tumor in his kidney. Lundgren had surgery to remove the tumor and continued appearing in movies like "Creed II" and "Aquaman." After remaining cancer-free for five years, doctors discovered more tumors in 2020. He later learned the cancer had spread to his liver, both lungs, spine and in and around his left kidney. "I had a lot of difficult conversations with myself," Lundgren told Fox News Digital. "I definitely had a few tough ones. Of course, as most older men do, you do estate planning. You plan your will and who's going to get what. But in this case, it was around the corner. It was something I had to plan a little more in detail, like funerals and trying to figure out where I would be, what would be better for my family. Planning your own funeral is kind of a saying, but I literally was doing that. That was tough." WATCH: DOLPH LUNDGREN OPENS UP ABOUT CANCER BATTLE, BECOMING US CITIZEN IN ‘FIGHTS WORTH FIGHTING’ During that time, Lundgren said he considered ending his life. "At some point, which was even harder, I started thinking, 'Do I really want to be in bed weighing 60 pounds and having people come and see me like that? Or should I just end it myself?'" Lundgren said. "I started considering that. I spoke to my brother. We made a deal, and he would help me out if it came to that, if I made that decision. But it was a tough conversation." In the book, Lundgren wrote, "When I was deep into the cancer treatments and thinking about the possibility of killing myself, my brother, Johan, was going to help me, because I didn’t know what kind of condition I might be in once I made that decision. I could be in really bad shape by then and not capable of completing the suicide on my own." "There are countries in Europe, like Switzerland, that permit legal suicide for people who are terminally ill, but I still might have needed someone there to help me," he continued. "Johan and I talked about it, but once I met Dr. Drakaki and began feeling a little better, it never went any further than that." Lundgren’s longtime friend Johan Pramell also said in the memoir that the star "wanted to go out in glory like a Viking because he didn't want people to have to watch him suffer or fade away." Medical aid in dying is not synonymous with euthanasia, according to the Online Journal of Issues in Nursing. The journal states that laws allowing medical aid in dying permit eligible adults with terminal illnesses to self-administer medication when certain criteria are met. According to Dignity in Dying, a U.K.-based advocacy organization, 10 countries in Europe have laws that allow people experiencing "unbearable suffering" to access assisted dying. But one thing was certain — Lundgren wasn't ready to die. "I have a certain discipline, a fighter's heart, since I was a kid," he told Fox News Digital. "I think that was helpful. I may have had these thoughts, but the other side of me wants to go another round to see what happens. Maybe the other guy will drop. You never know. I think that's a part of it." "But also, I believe being in good physical shape helped me, and continuing to work out through the whole thing," he said. "As much as I could, I would stay physically active. And then I was lucky to have my wife, who was very supportive, and my daughters." "They're the ones that kept me going by just their sheer presence," he added. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? Lundgren wrote in his memoir that he believed, based on the doctor's tone, his prognosis could have been closer to one or two years. After returning to Los Angeles, Lundgren sought a second opinion from Dr. Alexandra Drakaki, an oncologist at UCLA Health, whom he credited with saving his life. "At this point, I was depressed and had almost given up all hope," he wrote. According to the memoir, Drakaki determined that his cancer had been misdiagnosed, leading to a different treatment approach. "What she found was that my 'kidney cancer' cells had a mutation that is fairly common in lung cancer," he wrote. "That's why the medications I had been given for the past two years weren't working." After Lundgren went public with his cancer battle, one heavyweight stood in his corner: Sylvester Stallone. "Stallone and I have a long history, a good, long relationship together," he said. "We've known each other for 40 years. We've made six films together over that period. He went from being a mentor, a boss on set, director, producer. I was just a new kid on the block. And then slowly, we moved together and became more equals, I would say, two older guys who've been in the business a long time. And he has three daughters, I have two, and we share that as well." "When I got sick, he reached out to me," Lundgren said. "It was unexpected because he was the first one, actually, who reached out of everybody, even before some of my family, when it came out. And he was very emotional about it. It touched me. And that was another side of him that I'd never seen. Since then, we've been very close friends, even closer than before." In his memoir, he reflects on whether performance-enhancing drugs may have played a role in his cancer battle. Lundgren wrote that he used anabolic steroids and other performance-enhancing drugs on and off from 1986 to 1996 while preparing for physically demanding movie roles. While he stressed that there is "no conclusive evidence" the drugs caused his cancer, he acknowledged they "might have helped cause" it, adding that he could not say for certain. articles.title: 'She-Hulk' star slams Tom Selleck, Michael Jordan as 'cowardly' for avoiding political talk
articles.summary: Actress Tatiana Maslany called Tom Selleck and Michael Jordan "cowardly" for not using their celebrity platforms to speak out on political issues today.
articles.body: "She-Hulk" star Tatiana Maslany accused celebrities like Tom Selleck and Michael Jordan on Monday of behaving "cowardly" for not using their fame to push politics. Joining Mehdi Hasan on his podcast "We're Not Kidding with Mehdi & Friends," the Marvel TV actress was praised for her past support for the "Free Palestine" movement and accusing Israel of committing a "genocide" in Gaza. Maslany said that she believed it was her job as an artist to address political issues. "To me, artists are like mirrors to the world, to society," Maslany said. "We have to name things, whether it's emotional mirroring to people the human experience or it's speaking out or it's naming something. It's like such an important, intrinsic part of our job." MS RACHEL SAYS BACKLASH OVER HER GAZA POSTS 'DOESN'T FAZE' HER AS SHE CALLS OUT CELEBRITY SILENCE Hasan then asked what she thought about other celebrities staying silent on political issues, referencing a recent CNN interview with "Blue Bloods" and "Magnum P.I." actor Tom Selleck where he declined to discuss politics or NBA star Michael Jordan's famous "Republicans buy sneakers too" statement. "But all of it is political. Everything is political," Maslany responded. "All entertainment is political because it has a viewpoint and it has a perspective. It has visual representation of the world we live in or the kinds of things that are funny or acceptable or the ways that people relate to each other. It's all about inter-person, like there's no disconnect in my mind and to me, those are two very rich men who stand to lose a lot if they stand up for something." Hasan agreed with Maslany that celebrities were more concerned about "fewer opportunities to make money" by dabbling in political discussion, a sentiment Maslany called "bizarre" and "cowardly." DOLLY PARTON REFUSED TO PICK POLITICAL SIDES FOR DECADES: ‘I’M NOT IN POLITICS, I’M AN ENTERTAINER’ "Art should destabilize people, too. I'm not thinking, like Tom Selleck's going like ‘Magnum P.I. should really disturb people on a core level.' But like, art moves people, whether that's in like a shock way, a laughter way, all of it. It's a communication with the world ... It's such a bizarre mentality. It's so cowardly," Maslany said. In a comment to Fox News Digital, Media Research Center Video senior director Eric Scheiner called out Maslany for having the "typical leftist viewpoint that permeates Hollywood" and "the need to bully people into spouting forth a political opinion even when they choose not to." "Maslany and her irate ilk could learn from entertainment figures like Dolly Parton, whose recent passing was marked by loving tributes from everyone across the political and media spectrum," Scheiner said. "Parton quietly supported causes she believed in through private, personal actions. She never aired her politics on the public stage, because she wanted to entertain as many people as possible, not alienate a portion of her audience or encourage the ‘cancellation’ of those who disagreed with her." DWAYNE 'THE ROCK' JOHNSON BRANDED A COWARD BY HOLLYWOOD STARS AFTER REFUSING TO SPEAK OUT ON POLITICS "Maslany should just leave Selleck and Jordan alone, but much like any neighborhood Karen, she just can’t mind her own business," he added. articles.title: ‘Madden’ Trailer: Nicolas Cage Becomes the NFL’s Most Iconic Coach for David O. Russell
articles.summary: He's joined by Christian Bale, Kathryn Hahn, and John Mulaney in the Amazon MGM film, which opens on November 11.
articles.body:
Football season is in full swing — and even if a quarterback injury has already ended your team's season, you at least have a fall filled with football movies to look forward to. The most notable might be "Madden," David O. Russell's NFL biopic, which casts Nicolas Cage as one of the sport's most iconic figures.

Few personalities in sports history are as synonymous with their league as John Madden is with the NFL. As the head coach of the Oakland Raiders for nearly a decade, he secured his legacy as one of the game's great minds, winning the franchise's first Super Bowl and retiring with the greatest winning percentage of all time. He then spent the next four decades as a beloved color commentator, known for his distinct catchphrases and a love of Thanksgiving turducken. And of course, he licensed his name to a series of video games that remains one of the biggest properties in sports gaming, even years after his death.

His fruitful life should give Russell plenty to work with, and he lined up a cast that anyone would love to see in their own biopic. In addition to Cage, "Madden" stars Christian Bale as iconic Raiders owner Al Davis and an ensemble that includes Kathryn Hahn, John Mulaney, Sienna Miller, Joel Murray, and Shane Gillis.

"Madden" is co-written by Russell and Cambron Clark. Frequent Martin Scorsese and Quentin Tarantino collaborator Robert Richardson notably serves as cinematographer on the film. Producers include Todd Black, Jason Blumenthal, Jonathan Shukat, and Steve Tisch.

At one point, it appeared that "Madden" could be one of Cage's final movie roles, as he expressed a desire to wind down his film career and focus on television. But in a recent interview with IndieWire , he explained that making his TV debut on "Spider-Noir" restored his interest in film acting.

"Doing a season of television makes me interested in movies again. So I knew I had to try something else to reinvigorate and restimulate my process," he said. "And now I've done this and I'm happy with the results and I feel like I've learned something. I also feel like I have a little more confidence and I could see myself making more movies again."

An Amazon MGM release, "Madden" opens in select theaters on Friday, November 11 before streaming on Prime Video the following week. Watch the trailer below.

articles.summary: Veteran Bollywood actor Mushtaq Khan, a familiar face in Hindi cinema for over three decades, has died.
articles.body: Veteran Bollywood actor Mushtaq Khan, a familiar face in Hindi cinema for over three decades, has died. He passed away on Thursday evening, September 24, at Mumbai's Nanavati Hospital, where he had been admitted for the past 15 days. His business partner has confirmed that he had been battling cancer.Mushtaq Khan passes away at Nanavati HospitalAccording to an AajTak report, the 'Welcome' actor was taken to the hospital after his health worsened and was kept in the ICU. The report said he had been fighting cancer, which was first diagnosed five years ago and became serious again recently.His business partner, Shivam, confirmed the news to HT City. He said, "He (Mushtaq Khan) passed away around 7pm on Thursday. He had been detected with lung cancer earlier and had got well. However, it relapsed eight days back and had to be admitted to the hospital. It was last-stage cancer."Soon, actor-comedian Sunil Pal took to his Instagram Stories to mourn the demise of the veteran actor. Sharing a picture of Mushtaq Khan, Sunil Pal wrote, "RIP Mushtaq Khan saab."Meanwhile, Federation of Western India Cine Employees (FWICE) president BN Tiwari confirmed to ANI over the phone about his demise. He said, "Actor Mushtaq Khan died today.Television, theatre and comedyApart from cinema, Khan also worked in television and theatre. His comic timing and ease in supporting and character roles made him a well-known name among Hindi film viewers.Mushtaq Khan in 'Welcome'Mushtaq Khan’s portrayal of Ballu, Uday Shetty’s loyal sidekick in Akshay Kumar-starrer 'Welcome' (2007), remains one of the film’s most memorable comic characters. His deadpan delivery and hilarious backstory turned Ballu into an instant fan favourite. His iconic dialogue, “Meri ek taang nakli hai, main hockey ka bahut bada khiladi tha,” became hugely popular and continues to be quoted and shared by fans.His association with Mahesh BhattIn an interview published in August 2026, Khan spoke about his early struggles. He said Salim Khan's recommendation helped him secure a meeting with filmmaker Mahesh Bhatt, which led to his role in 'Kabzaa' (1988). He went on to work with Bhatt in several films, including 'Aashiqui', 'Dil Hai Ki Manta Nahin', 'Saathi', 'Sadak', 'Junoon', 'Gunaah', 'Sir' and 'Hum Hain Rahi Pyar Ke'.A career spanning several decadesKhan began acting in films in the 1980s and appeared in many popular movies across genres. He was best known as Gul Khan, also called Gullu, in the 'Gadar' franchise. He shared the screen with Sunny Deol in 'Gadar: Ek Prem Katha' (2001) and returned to the role more than two decades later in 'Gadar 2' (2023).His other notable films include 'Aashiqui' (1990), 'Dil Hai Ki Manta Nahin' (1991), 'Sadak' (1991), 'Hum Hain Rahi Pyar Ke' (1993), 'Krantiveer' (1994), 'Raja' (1995), 'Jodi No. 1' (2001), 'Mujhse Shaadi Karogi' (2004), 'Welcome' (2007), 'Wanted' (2009), 'Oh My God!' (2012), 'Stree' (2018) and 'Stree 2' (2024).FamilyThe veteran actor is survived by his family. He was married to Salma Khan, and the couple have children, including sons Mohammed Arshad Khan and Mohshin Khan. Arshad is married to Saba Khan, a teacher, while Mohshin has worked as a model.Film industry in shockThe news has shocked the film industry, especially as the actor had remained active in recent years. With roles spanning comedy, drama and character-driven parts, Mushtaq Khan was among the best-known supporting actors of his generation. articles.body:
Macklemore has announced the "Free Palestine" tour, with three shows set for Dublin (Oct. 26), Paris (Oct. 29) and London (Oct. 30). The news comes after the Grammy-winning rapper was infamously dropped as opener from Ed Sheeran's U.S. tour after making "Free Palestine" speeches while on stage at two concerts at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey.

Per Live Nation, the "Free Palestine" tour will "bring Macklemore together with artists and friends for a series of performances that center Palestine and Palestinians, and help provide humanitarian aid and support to the movement."

Additionally, all proceeds from the concerts will benefit the following organizations: Anera, Glia, Gaza Soup Kitchen, Taawon, HEAL Palestine, Palestinian Youth Movement, Middle East Children's Alliance, Jewish Voice for Peace, Medical Aid for Palestinians. Institute for Middle East Understanding, Palestine Children's Relief Fund and UNRWA USA.

"If these last couple of weeks have shown us anything, it's that something has shifted over the last three years," Macklemore wrote in a statement on Instgaram while announcing the tour. "There has been a collective awakening around Palestinian liberation, the power of billionaires that try to censor that call, and what we expect from artists right now."

"It's 2026. Being apolitical during a genocide doesn't work anymore," he continued. "People are asking artists to show up, educate themselves and be in community. To use the stage for more than entertainment. To push back when the call for a Free Palestine is met with attempts to silence it… What happened to me is bigger than one artist or one stage. When the billionaire class can decide which voices are allowed on stage and which ones are too dangerous to hear, everyone should be paying attention."

Macklemore said that New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft “rallied” other stadium owners after taking issue with his “Free Palestine” remarks during a show. Sheeran confirmed that Kraft was among those who called him after Macklemore performed his anti-war song and the speech that preceded it at Metlife Stadium circulated online. The situation surrounding Macklemore, Sheeran and Kraft made international headlines this month as many debated not just Macklemore’s speech regarding the Israel-Gaza war, but also the rights for artists to express their views. It began when Macklemore joined Sheeran’s “Loop” tour in New Jersey and performed “Hind’s Hall,” his song inspired by the anti-war protests at Columbia University in 2024. Macklemore made a speech prior to the performance that called for a “Free Palestine” and also told Jewish members of the audience that his comments regarding the Israeli government was in no way about them. The performance of “Hind’s Hall” also had related images from pro-Palestinian demonstrations and the situation in Gaza. Kraft did not deny allegations made by Macklemore in his own statement earlier this month, but said Gillette Stadium — which his entertainment group owns — seeks to create a welcoming environment for everyone. He took issue with Macklemore’s actions at the New Jersey show and “and a broader history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery that we believe has been deeply offensive and hurtful to the Jewish community.” “Much of my time and attention for the last decade has been focused on the fight against antisemitism and hate of all kinds, and I feel a responsibility to stand up when I believe that line has been crossed,” Kraft said. The Patriots owner also said he was not trying to stifle Palestinian advocacy or diminish the suffering of Palestinians. Kraft did not specifically reference past actions of concern from Macklemore, but many online brought up a 2014 incident in which Macklemore wore a costume that appeared to play on antisemitic tropes: a wig, a fake beard and a hooked nose. He wore it to the Grammys that year, saying at the time that he thought it would be fun to dress in disguise to talk to fans. Macklemore apologized after the antisemitic stereotype was pointed out, saying he had been in touch with the Anti-Defamation League, an organization founded to combat antisemitism. The ADL accepted the apology at the time, saying it took him “at his word that he did not have any ill intent,” according to The Guardian. Ed Sheeran backlash Sheeran faced a wave of backlash over his role in the situation as some commenters felt that the singer should have taken a stance on the war or at least Macklemore’s right to speak on his opinion. All of Sheeran’s opening acts, as well as his house band, dropped out of their scheduled U.S. tour dates in solidarity with Macklemore and the Palestinian people. The “Perfect” singer initially released a statement explaining his side of the situation and clarifying that it was not his choice to drop Macklemore. Sheeran said that his promoters, who held the contract with Macklemore, made the decision as he attempted to build bridges with venue owners. Sheeran went on with his scheduled concert in Philadelphia on Saturday, tearfully addressing the crowd who showed up in spite of the criticism he faced. “I’ve never wanted to be an activist musician,” Sheeran said. “But this has put me in the middle of an important and passionate argument about freedom of speech and the most complex political issue on the planet.” Israel launched its offensive in the Gaza Strip after the Hamas-led attacks on Israel on Oct. 7, 2023, in which about 1,200 people were killed and roughly 250 others were taken hostage. More than 73,000 people have been killed in Gaza during Israel’s military campaign, including at least 1,200 since a fragile ceasefire took effect in October, according to the Palestinian Health Ministry. Sheeran acknowledged the “horrific” Oct. 7 attack on Israel by Hamas which started the war, but went on to say what has happened in Gaza as a result is “catastrophic and unjustifiable and disproportionate.” “This is a humanitarian issue and I cannot hide how I feel about it anymore,” he said.

articles.title: Johnny Depp Continues His Hollywood Return in First Trailer for “Day Drinker” with Penélope Cruz and Madelyn Cline
articles.summary: ‘Day Drinker’ is in theaters March 26, 2027
articles.body:
Johnny Depp is continuing his return to Hollywood in his new movie Day Drinker , which just released its first trailer on Thursday, Sept. 24

The Marc Webb-directed film also stars Penélope Cruz and Madelyn Cline

This fall's Ebeneezer and Day Drinker will serve as Depp's first two films from a major distributor since 2018

Johnny Depp is continuing his return to Hollywood in Day Drinker .

Lionsgate released the first trailer for the upcoming action-thriller from director Marc Webb , which costars Penélope Cruz and Madelyn Cline alongside Depp, 63. Cline, 28, portrays a bartender on a private yacht who serves a mysterious guest in Depp's lead character, who appears to be an Australian man and — perhaps — also a vampire.

"A private-yacht bartender encounters a mysterious, onboard guest (Johnny Depp)," reads an official synopsis for the movie. "They soon find themselves entangled with a criminal figure (Cruz, 54) and connected in ways no one saw coming."

Written by Zach Dean, Day Drinker will mark Depp's second film from a major distributor since Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald (2018). Since the end of his highly publicized defamation trial with ex-wife Amber Heard in 2022, he has starred in the French film Jeanne du Barry , which opened the 2023 Cannes Film Festival and directed the film Modi: Three Days on the Wing of Madness . This November, Depp will star in the upcoming adaptation of A Christmas Carol titled Ebeneezer .

Day Drinker also marks the fourth big-screen collaboration between Depp and Cruz after Blow (2001), Pirates of the Caribbean: On Stranger Tides (2011) and Murder on the Orient Express (2017). Aside from Depp, Cline and Cruz, the Day Drinker cast also includes Manu Ríos, Arón Piper, Juan Diego Botto and Anika Boyle. Director Webb ( Snow White ), 50, previously said in a statement, "I'm excited to be starting production with Johnny, Madelyn, Penélope and this incredible cast."

Back in June 2025, Depp and Cruz were seen stepping out together in June at the Museo Reina Sofía in Madrid, where they posed in front of Picasso's Guernica . Two photos shared by the museum in a joint Instagram post with Depp showed the actor and his frequent collaborator dressed in casual-elegant attire for a smiley selfie and a further-away shot.

"We're in a beautiful location with a fantastic crew and a thrilling, ferocious story to tell," Webb added at the time. "This is gonna be fun."

articles.title: Sharon Stone Says "Euphoria" Costar Sydney Sweeney Should 'Take Responsibility' for Her Nude Sports Betting Ad (Exclusive)
articles.summary: Stone spoke about the controversy at 'Variety''s 2026 Power of Women event, which took place on Wednesday, Sept. 23, at the Beverly Hills Hotel in L.A.
articles.body:
During an appearance at Variety's 2026 Power of Women event, Sharon Stone criticized Sydney Sweeney's nearly nude ad for sports betting platform Novig

Female athletes, including Amy Hunt and Gracie Kramer, have also publicly condemned the ad as harmful to women in sports

Stone previously weighed in on Sweeney during a 2025 controversy surrounding her American Eagle jeans campaign

Sharon Stone is discussing her Euphoria costar Sydney Sweeney 's controversial sports betting ad for Novig .

Speaking exclusively to PEOPLE at Variety's 2026 Power of Women: Los Angeles event on Wednesday, Sept. 23, at the Beverly Hills Hotel, Stone, 68, said that Sweeney, 29, needs to "take responsibility" for the campaign, which sparked a backlash among female athletes.

In the ad, Sweeney bared almost all as she promised viewers that the new app would be "just sports." "Just you, your takes and sports," a topless Sweeney tells the camera at one point while holding her breasts.

"I think that it's up to her to take responsibility for her actions, not up to me to judge her for her actions. It is up to me to be a cheerleader for the women who have made it through and become champions in women's sports," the Basic Instinct star adds.

"We can't denigrate women's sports to get men's attention so they can gamble," the Oscar nominee continues about the ad for Novig, which shows Sweeney in a number of provocative positions with sports equipment as she encourages viewers to use Novig for betting predictions for the NBA, NFL and more.

Stone goes on to note to PEOPLE that while in high school, she threatened to sue if she wasn't allowed to try out for the boys' golf team, given that there weren't any women's sports teams at her school.

"I had something to prove," Stone says, adding that she successfully "made the boys' team."

This isn't the first time that Stone has waded in on one of Sweeney's controversies.

At Variety 's Power of Women event in October 2025, she commented on her former costar Sweeney in the wake of the younger actress' American Eagle jeans campaign that sparked controversy that summer.

"It's okay to use what mama gave you. It's really fine," the Catwoman star said at the time.

"It's hard to be hot, and I think we all know that. It's really okay to use every bit of hotness you have — right here, right now — and go for whatever that is, because everybody has their own certain kind of hotness, their own certain thing, and you're supposed to go for that. Because who are you not to be beautiful? You know, who you are isn't an accident."

At the time, the American Eagle campaign and its "good jeans" tagline sparked debate on social media . Some claimed that the usage of the word "jeans" as a play on "genes" is racially charged and hints at genetic superiority. Others criticized the campaign for catering to the male gaze and taking inspiration from Brooke Shields' controversial 1980 denim campaign.

However, American Eagle told critics that the ad campaign was " always was about the jeans " and that "great jeans look good on everyone."

After the controversy, American Eagle's stock surged by 25%, according to a report by CNN.

Elsewhere, several female athletes have been quick to call out Sweeney's Novig ad , with one Olympian calling it a "massive step backward" for women.

In a post-race interview with BBC Sport after the Ultimate Championship on Sept. 13, British track star Amy Hunt said, "Sydney Sweeney, this is what women in sport look like."

American gymnast Gracie Kramer, meanwhile, called out Sweeney via TikTok, writing , "Idk what Sydney Sweeney was doing, but this is what a woman in sports looks like," over a highlight reel of herself on the mat.

Kramer, 28, also penned a stern message about the ad in a post on her Instagram Stories, calling it "infuriating."

She also slammed the ad for marketing women's sports "through the male gaze" and called it "a massive step backward."

"We should not have to take our clothes off to convince men that women belong in sports," Kramer added.

articles.title: NAZA, Israeli film on Gaza, to stream for free after theatrical run
articles.summary: Co-director Yuval Abraham says documentary exposing Israeli abuses will be available online in November.
articles.body:
A documentary that accuses Israel of using AI to carry out mass civilian killings in Gaza will be available to stream online for free once its theatrical rollout in more than 50 countries is complete.

Israeli filmmaker Yuval Abraham, who co-directed NAZA with fellow Israeli filmmaker Rachel Szor, announced on Thursday that viewers will be able to stream the award-winning film from November on The Guardian’s website. The UK newspaper helped produce the film.

“I know there is enormous demand to watch the film, and I hope that in this way, everyone will soon be able to see it: whether in cinemas or online in a few weeks,” Abraham said in a post on X.

“We made the film to spark a public discussion about the [Israeli] government’s actions in Gaza, the killing of more than 73,000 people, most of them civilians, the normalisation of a war of extermination, of the notion that ‘there are no uninvolved’,” he added.

NAZA, which means “collateral damage” in Hebrew, will premiere in the United States on Saturday at the New York Film Festival.

The documentary is also due to premiere in several other countries, including the United Kingdom, France, Germany and Canada.

NAZA is 80 minutes long and is the result of a nearly three-year investigation into Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza. The documentary is based on testimony from Israeli military and intelligence sources whose identities have been concealed.

One of the film’s subjects described the process of using AI to kill Palestinians in the enclave as “insanely fun” and said it was like playing a “video game”. Another described it as a “mission”.

The sources explain in detail an AI system called Lavender , which they said was used to identify assassination targets.

Israel oversees a system of mass surveillance in Gaza, monitoring people’s phone calls, movements and interactions. Lavender allegedly uses this data when deciding who to assassinate and is believed to have an error rate of up to 10 percent.

According to another of the film’s subjects, an attack was approved despite knowledge that as many as 500 civilians could be killed.

NAZA was awarded the Special Jury Prize at this year’s Venice International Film Festival .

Israel has been condemned by several human rights organisations for its atrocities in Gaza. Amnesty International and Doctors Without Borders, known by its French acronym MSF, among others, say Israel is committing a genocide.

Earlier this month, Israeli Culture Minister Miki Zoha called for Abraham and Szor to be stripped of their citizenship and accused them of “treason”. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has since pledged to pass a law that would revoke the citizenship of anyone who defames ⁠⁠Israeli soldiers.

In his post on X, Abraham said: “Journalism is not betrayal. Criticism is not betrayal. It is the duty of every citizen whose government commits crimes to know, and of every soldier who witnessed them to tell.”

He said “thousands” of Israeli soldiers will “watch the film and recognise what is described in it personally”.

“Even if it’s frightening, it is your duty to find a way to testify to what you saw,” Abraham said.

articles.title: Making it as a musician: 'Vital to make connections' if you want to play a festival
articles.summary: Industry experts have been telling BBC News NI how to pitch yourself to a festival.
articles.body:
As the festival season comes to an end, budding musicians may be wondering "how can I get on stage?".

Well the answers would be, do your homework, make connections and be involved in the "community".

That's the advice industry professionals such as bookers, agents and festival bosses have been handing out at a music conference in Belfast on Thursday.

Ross Parkhill, from the Stendhal Festival, said those things are "vital".

The Stendhal Festival is one of Northern Ireland's largest annual independent music and arts festivals and Parkhill said "presentation" is everything when it comes to pitching yourself to a festival.

"How you present yourself, we do an application process every year and the narrative you build around, in your bio or via email, how you present yourself and being real," he told BBC News NI at the Output Belfast conference.

He said "asking questions, being personable and building a connection is the vital stuff".

And connections is something that is echoed by other festival organisers, such as Megan Evans from The Deer Shed Festival in Yorkshire.

She said it is "important" to "understand the festival" when pitching to them.

"We get a lot of submissions every year so it is really important that you think about how you are pitching to us."

In the age of social media, it may seem easy to create connections, however Evans said a "balance" is needed.

"I definitely think it has changed the landscape. I talk to a lot of independent artists about the balance of live experience and also gaining that following on social media and how you manage that and not being a slave to it."

So what is the experience like for artists trying to break into the scene?

Ewan McElhinney and Alex Talbot are bandmates.

McElhinney said he was at the conference to "learn more" about the industry and "promote" the band.

He said that while his band had pitched to festivals before, the panel discussion on pitching yourself was "very interesting, very helpful".

"It is something we are interested in doing in the future, so it was very informative."

Talbot added that it was good to hear from different backgrounds on how to pitch for festivals.

"It was a cohesive understand of that process that it is people behind the screen each time, which sometimes you forget when you are sending like a million emails."

For booking agent Angie Rance she said it important to have experience when you pitch yourself to a festival.

"It is a big part of any artists career... it is a big part of building an artist."

She said "grafting and pitching" is a big part of the work she does.

articles.title: Dolly Parton’s estate lawsuit claims nephew Bryan Seaver said he sold $27 million worth of ammunition and arms to Haitian police on the day the singer died: Report
articles.summary: Nearly one month after Dolly Parton’s death on August 25, her estate has become embroiled in a legal dispute involving her nephew and longtime head of
articles.body: Nearly one month after Dolly Parton’s death on August 25, her estate has become embroiled in a legal dispute involving her nephew and longtime head of security, Bryan Seaver. According to court documents obtained by PEOPLE, Seaver has been accused of attempting to extract money from She’s Alive, LLC., the entity Parton established to protect her professional property and business interests after her death. The filings also allege that he made increasingly threatening statements toward people involved in managing the estate.Seaver was terminated as Parton’s head of security earlier this month. He has denied threatening anyone and disputed the characterization of his private conversations, saying some of the comments cited in the lawsuit were taken out of context. He also called the temporary restraining order “spurious” and “simply a publicity stunt” in a statement to ABC News.What did Bryan Seaver allegedly say?The court filing claims that, in conversations with Parton’s longtime manager Danny Nozell, Seaver sought to create “fear and chaos” while attempting to obtain money for his personal benefit.The lawsuit alleges that Seaver made statements about retaliation against people he believed had betrayed his family. One message cited in the filing allegedly referenced weapons, his military background and what he described as his willingness to pursue those he felt had wronged his family.The documents also allege that Seaver sent a September 3 email to an entertainment attorney who had worked with Parton for years. In that message, he reportedly claimed that he had sold $27 million worth of ammunition and arms to Haitian police on the day Parton died and described himself as an “international arms dealer and mercenary.”Seaver says comments were taken out of contextSeaver has strongly disputed the allegations. He told ABC News that he had “never threatened anyone” and said the people involved were his friends, colleagues and brothers.He also addressed the allegation that he described himself as a “killer.” Seaver said the term had a different meaning within Parton’s circle and was an inside joke.“Dolly called me her killer. It was a joke we used around her camp,” he said, arguing that Nozell had taken the comment out of context.In a separate statement shared with TMZ, Seaver said he was a security professional and acknowledged using the word “killer,” but maintained that the messages were private conversations between two people grieving Parton’s death.Bryan Seaver announced Dolly Parton’s deathThe allegations come after Seaver was the person who publicly announced Parton’s death on August 25. He said in the video that Parton had asked him years earlier to share the news when the time came.“As her head of security for more than two decades, a role my father Larry held before me, I have imagined the heaviness of this moment but haven’t truly felt it until now,” Seaver said at the time.Seaver had worked as Parton’s head of security for more than two decades, taking over a position previously held by his father, Larry.Why was Seaver removed from his security role?The lawsuit alleges that the situation escalated to a point where several people associated with Parton’s estate felt unsafe. According to the filing, the trusts and estates attorney handling Parton’s affairs resigned after allegedly receiving harassing and ominous communications.The documents further claim that other employees resigned rather than risk retaliation and that some personnel began avoiding the office.Seaver has rejected those allegations and said he was fired over what he described as “contrived threats.”Dolly Parton’s sister defends SeaverThe legal dispute has also prompted a response from Parton’s family. Her sister Freida Parton defended Seaver in a Facebook statement on September 23 and said there was “no feud” within the family.“No one among the Parton/Owens family is fighting over Dolly’s estate,” she wrote, adding that the family loves Seaver as they love one another.Her statement comes as the lawsuit focuses on the alleged conduct involving Seaver, She’s Alive and the management of Parton’s professional interests rather than establishing a dispute among Parton’s relatives.What happens next in the Dolly Parton estate case?The temporary restraining order limits Seaver and members of his security company from contacting or approaching certain employees, attorneys and business associates connected to She’s Alive. A hearing is scheduled for October 7.The allegations remain claims made in court filings and have not been established as facts at trial. Seaver has denied threatening anyone and maintains that several of the statements cited in the lawsuit were taken out of context.
