articles.title: While Millennials cheer Toys R Us comeback, key piece of data reveals dystopian reason for its return
articles.summary: Toys R Us plans to open 120 new stores this holiday season, but surging adult toy sales among millennials are driving the iconic retailer's comeback.
articles.body: If you came of age in the 80s or 90s, chances are you remember Toys R Us, the international toy retailer with the anthropomorphic giraffe for a mascot and the catchiest jingle in the business. "I don't wanna grow up, I wanna be a Toys R Us kid." Well, the truth of the matter is we did grow up, and about a decade ago, millennials aging out of the toy-buying demographic spelled doom for the once-titanic toy store, as Toys R Us filed for bankruptcy in 2017 and closed all of their stores the following year. 'TOY STORY 5' REVIEW: TOM HANKS, TIM ALLEN RETURN FOR TIMELY INSTALLMENT AS PIXAR GANG BATTLES RISE OF TECH But then, just recently, something unexpected happened. Toys R Us started to make a comeback, first as a part of larger retail stores like Macy's, and then, little by little, as standalone shops in malls and airports. THE NINTENDO 64 IS TURNING 30 YEARS OLD, HERE ARE SOME OF ITS MOST IMPACTFUL GAMES OF ALL TIME Now, Toys R Us is set to open 120 stores across the country this holiday season, bringing its total number of standalone U.S. stores to 160. Hang on just a second, though. Did you read the last part of that post? "As toy sales surge among adult shoppers," reads like there are a bunch of losers in their 30s and 40s pacing up and down the aisles of their local toy stores while shoving kids out of the way for the last Funko Pop. But surely that's not the case here, right? This is just a bunch of older Millennials with kids of their own passing on their love of toys and games to the next generation. Right? Yep, I knew it. It looks like the only reason Toys R Us is making a comeback is because a bunch of 90s kids who are now old enough to have kids of their own took that aforementioned jingle a little too literally. I know you "wanna be a Toys R Us kid," but you're 36 years old. It's time to let someone a little younger have a crack at the LEGO Star Wars set. I don't know what it is with my generation and having a serious case of arrested development, but they're almost allergic to acting their age. Listen, I'm not saying you're not allowed to have some of the same hobbies you had when you were 13. WE GREW UP BEFORE SCREENS TOOK OVER. OUR KIDS DESERVE THAT CHANCE TOO Hell, I will still hop on the Xbox to blow off a little steam or watch movies and TV shows from my youth. But I also haven't been spending chunks of my salary on toys and video games for most of my adult life, and I donated all my Pokemon cards to kids at the summer camp I used to work at back in college. If I have bought a toy in the past two years, it was for my son, and that's the disheartening thing about these numbers. Instead of passing the "kid hobbies" torch, Millennials are just hoarding it to themselves. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Nostalgia is a powerful agent, one that I have been known to write about frequently, but there's a fine line between showing reverence for "the good old days" and outright refusing to live in the present. It's a ton of fun to see my son's eyes light up whenever he opens the package to a Spider-Man figure or a Bluey plushy, but I couldn't imagine someone with a beard and a car payment getting the same satisfaction from that. It all feels weird and a little dystopian. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER I'll be excited to take my son to Toys R Us when one opens near me, just as my dad did when I was a kid, but the joy will be vicarious. articles.title: Macklemore slammed as 'performative' after announcing 'Free Palestine Tour'
articles.summary: Macklemore announced a "Free Palestine Tour" with shows in Dublin, Paris and London after being dropped from Ed Sheeran's tour over his performances.
articles.body: Macklemore is taking his views on Palestine on the road. The rapper, who was dropped from Ed Sheeran's tour earlier this month after stirring controversy with his politically charged performances, announced Thursday that he's going on a new tour he's calling the "Free Palestine Tour." articles.title: Roberto Bosquet, chef, desvela la receta “fácil, saludable y brutal” que se prepara en menos de 15 minutos
articles.standfirst: Una propuesta sencilla que apenas requiere tiempo en la cocina
articles.summary: Una propuesta sencilla que apenas requiere tiempo en la cocina
articles.body: Comer saludable no siempre implica pasar horas entre fogones. Roberto Bosquet, conocido por compartir recetas sencillas y equilibradas, ha vuelto a demostrarlo con una propuesta que se puede preparar en apenas 15 minutos y que combina legumbres, verduras y proteínas. La receta parte de ingredientes muy habituales y no requiere elaboraciones complicadas. Solo hacen falta 200 gramos de garbanzos cocidos, 100 gramos de tomates cherry, tres huevos y algunos condimentos como aceite de oliva virgen extra, sal, pimienta, orégano y cúrcuma. El primer paso consiste en colocar los garbanzos cocidos y los tomates cherry, previamente cortados por la mitad, en un recipiente. Después se añade un poco de aceite de oliva y se incorporan las especias al gusto. Una vez mezclados todos los ingredientes, se colocan en una bandeja y se introducen en el horno. Bosquet propone hornear la mezcla durante unos 15 minutos a 200 grados. También existe la posibilidad de utilizar una freidora de aire, ajustando el tiempo en función de cómo se vaya tostando la preparación para evitar que se haga demasiado. Mientras los garbanzos y los tomates están en el horno, se pueden preparar los tres huevos a la plancha. Una vez terminada la cocción, solo queda servir la mezcla en un plato, añadir los huevos por encima y decorar al gusto. El resultado es una combinación sencilla que reúne diferentes grupos de alimentos en un mismo plato y que puede funcionar tanto para una comida rápida como para una cena. El chef define su propuesta como una idea “fácil, saludable y brutal” y anima a no complicar en exceso la alimentación diaria. “A veces nos ponemos varias mentales que nos dicen que todo es complicado, pero la verdad es que se puede disfrutar en este caso de algo rico y saludable, sin esfuerzo y sin perder el tiempo”, explica. Con pocos ingredientes, apenas unos minutos y una preparación muy sencilla, esta receta se presenta como una alternativa para quienes buscan comer bien sin convertir la cocina en una tarea interminable.

articles.summary: MUMBAI: Senior film, TV and stage actor Mushtaq Khan passed away of cancer at age 76 in Mumbai Thursday.
articles.body: MUMBAI: Senior film, TV and stage actor Mushtaq Khan passed away of cancer at age 76 in Mumbai Thursday.The tall strapping comedian brought a spark to the big and small screen, shuffling sideways as he walked, pulling up his trousers and rolling his eyes as he muttered funny one-liners.Khan had been admitted to Nanavati Hospital since a fortnight.BN Tiwari, president of FWICE (Federation of Western India Cine Employees) told TOI, "He was an artiste of great calibre and a pleasant, affable person. Just six months ago our union helped him recover old dues which a producer owed him. He was undergoing medical treatment at the time."Khan started his film career with Albert Pinto Ko Gussa Kyon Aata Hai in the mid-70s, then drew attention in Mahesh Bhatt films like Aashiqui, Dil Hai Ki Manta Nahin and Sadak. Khan's comic timing in Hum Hain Rahi Pyar Ke, Jodi No 1, and Welcome, where he played a disabled hockey player, brought the house down.The serials Wagle Ki Duniya, Chamatkar, Tedhe Medhe Sapne were other highlights. Khan remained circuit active on the OTT circuit as well.He is survived by his wife and two sons.Mushtaq Khan was born in 1950 in Baihar village, Madhya Pradesh, and lived there until he completed his MA from Balaghat nearby.He told this reporter in 2019, "I was fond of acting from childhood. I was in class six when I began to perform and sing in school plays. I did some mono acting as well. I cultivated a desire to become a film actor in college where I wrote, acted and directed my own plays."Khan's father was a garment dealer who was not happy at his son aiming for cinema. However, his elder brother was supportive.“And then something happened which compelled my father to back my passion. One day a serious fight broke out between a group of students from my college and some policemen. I think a couple of policemen even died of their wounds. The incident blew up and became a talking point. My father felt it was best to send me away from there lest I be drawn into the controversy. I took my chance and came away to Bombay,” he added.Mushtaq Khan had a friend named Suresh Zargar who guided him to the Bharatiya Jan Natya Manch (later IPTA) to channelise his talent."I began to get good work. I did a play called ‘Dronacharya’ by Shankar Shesh which received wide acclaim," he had said.In 2024, Khan claimed he was abducted on the Delhi-Meerut highway, with kidnappers demanding a ransom of Rs 1 crore. articles.title: The ‘Amazing Race’ star, Tim Janus, passes away at 49 after a long battle with cancer
articles.summary: Tim Janus, known as 'Eater X', passed away at 49 after a long cancer battle. The competitive eating star and former 'Amazing Race' contestant's life was marked by incredible food challenges and surprising adventures. Discover the full story of his unique legacy.
articles.body: Tim Janus, popularly known to competitive-eating fans as 'Eater X,' passed away at 49. The former 'Amazing Race' contestant breathed his last on September 16, 2026, following complications from a long battle with cancer, according to Major League Eating.Janus' story was never just about how much food he could eat. Behind the painted face, Viking-inspired mask and larger-than-life competitive persona was a man whose interests ranged from reality television and game shows to wildlife adventures, whistling and even a possible career in the US Foreign Service.Who was Tim Janus?He was born on December 31, 1976, in Simsbury, Connecticut. His early years gave little indication that he would eventually make a name for himself in competitive eating. After earning a degree in political science and public policy from Southern Methodist University, he later made New York City's East Village his home.In 2006, his life took an unexpected turn. Janus entered the world of competitive eating and quickly became one of its recognisable personalities. Over the years, he rose to No. 2 in the world rankings, behind Joey Chestnut. His appearance was impossible to miss, featuring painted designs on his face and a Viking-style mask. Janus developed the “Eater X” persona that became closely associated with him.From tiramisu to ramen, Tim Janus's eating records were unusualJanus wasn't known for competing in just one type of food contest. His career included championships involving desserts, noodles and sushi.According to Major League Eating, he became a world tiramisu-eating champion after consuming four pounds in six minutes. He also won a world ramen noodle-eating championship after eating 10.5 pounds in eight minutes.Then came sushi. Janus became a world nigiri sushi champion after consuming 141 pieces in six minutes. He also competed at the famous Nathan's Famous Fourth of July hot dog eating contest, one of the most recognisable events in competitive eating.Yet Janus seemed to see the sport as something bigger than simply setting records. During his induction into the Major League Eating Hall of Fame, he said, “I tell people that I learned a lot about life by eating hot dogs and I mean it. If you care about something and work hard at it, it makes you better.”How did Tim Janus land on ‘The Amazing Race’?Janus' competitive spirit eventually took him somewhere far removed from an eating table. In 2018, he teamed up with Joey Chestnut for Season 30 of The Amazing Race. The pair swapped food challenges for international travel, physical tasks and unfamiliar situations.Their journey ended with an eighth-place finish. But 'The Amazing Race' wasn't Janus' only television appearance. He competed on Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?, where he won $100,000. He also appeared on Cash Cab, reportedly becoming the show's biggest winner at the time after taking home $1,600.The side of ‘Eater X’ many people may not knowPerhaps the most surprising part of Janus' story was everything he did outside competitive eating. Major League Eating recalled some of the unusual experiences he pursued during his life. He travelled to Australia to track crocodiles and snakes in the wild. He milked a cow. He even appeared as a television weatherman. And then there was his whistling talent.Janus reportedly had a repertoire that included Neil Diamond songs and the Hartford Whalers' fight song. At one point, he was also accepted into the United States Foreign Service and received an assignment. His plans to work abroad, however, were affected by his illness. For someone famous for eating enormous quantities of food, his interests were surprisingly difficult to categorize.Friends remember Tim Janus beyond the recordsFollowing his death, tributes focused on the person behind the “Eater X” character. Crazy Legs Conti, a fellow competitive eater and Janus' former roommate, remembered him as someone who followed his own path rather than worrying about conventional expectations.Conti described Janus as “unique, brilliant and beloved by his friends.”Major League Eating also remembered his curiosity and his willingness to pursue whatever caught his attention. Janus is survived by his mother, Lucinda Hannon, his father, Peter Janus, his stepmother, Nancy Janus and his sister, Tess McNair.Major League Eating said a celebration of life is planned in New York City in October.For many viewers, Tim Janus may always be remembered as the eccentric “Eater X” who competed alongside Joey Chestnut on The Amazing Race. articles.body: Nani's 'The Paradise' opened its theatrical run with a strong collection on Thursday, September 24. According to Sacnilk, the action drama earned Rs 34.65 cr in India net on Day 1.The film recorded the collection through 9,732 shows. This takes the worldwide gross of 'The Paradise' to Rs 74.90 cr after its first day.'The Paradise' records 198.7% growthThe Day 1 India net collection was 198.7% higher than the Rs 11.60 cr earned through advance sales. The pre-sales were recorded on Day 0, September 23. The advance bookings were spread across 900 shows. It also pointed to shortcomings in the second half."What makes The Paradise frustrating is that the first half has already shown us the better film hiding within it. The world is compelling. articles.title: Meet 'the devil': Actor who plays Satan, Judas Iscariot shares power of comedy in uncertain political times
articles.summary: Jarret LeMaster has played Satan and Adolf Hitler but now voices Bumblebee in the Transformers 40th anniversary short alongside Frank Welker.
articles.body: Jarret LeMaster has played some sinister roles as Satan, Adolf Hitler and Judas Iscariot, but now he's stepping into one of pop culture's most beloved franchises as Bumblebee. The Christian actor, writer and former worship leader voices the Autobots in "Optimus Prime: Awakening," the new animated short accompanying the 40th anniversary theatrical rerelease of "The Transformers: The Movie." But LeMaster told Fox News Digital there is one thing he would rather not do on camera: kiss another woman. "I don't wanna kiss anybody, and, so, playing bad guys makes a lot of sense for me," LeMaster said. "They never kiss anybody, you know. They just murder them. BILLY BALDWIN ADMITS HE REFUSED TO KISS CO-STAR AFTER WEEKS OF TENSION ON SET "When you're murdering somebody, you're always pretending," he continued. "When you're kissing someone, you are always actually kissing them. And, so, you know, that's my line. I don't wanna cross that line. "Playing bad guys really works for my family," he joked. "And then my kids can look up to me as a great villain." It's an unusual résumé for someone who spent years working in church ministry. LeMaster said he still volunteers and leads worship at his local church, although he tends to keep some of his acting work "on the DL." SKILLET’S JOHN COOPER SAYS CHRISTIANS WHO CALL ROCK MUSIC ‘DEMONIC’ ARE ‘GETTING THE GOSPEL WRONG’ "Sometimes people are upset that I play 'Woke Jesus.' Sometimes people think that it's weird that I played the devil. Sometimes people were offended that I would, you know, play Adolf Hitler," he said. "The one that is not offensive is Bumblebee. People are very excited about that for some reason." LeMaster's path from church ministry to professional villain began when he got a call one day asking him to play a Russian murderer in a sketch for Christian satire outlet The Babylon Bee. "We need a Russian murderer. You kind of look like that," LeMaster recalled being told. At the time, he was working full time at his church and with the Bee. He initially assumed the company must be based somewhere like "Idaho or Narnia," only to discover it was in California. 'THE PASSION OF THE CHRIST' RETURNS TO THEATERS IN 4K WITH A 'RESURRECTION OF THE CHRIST' SNEAK PEEK One villain eventually led to another. "I don't know why I always get cast as bad characters," LeMaster said. "I think it's probably just because I'm bald. ... I blame the media. I blame [actor] Jason Statham." His latest role puts LeMaster firmly on the other side of the good-versus-evil divide. "Optimus Prime: Awakening" features LeMaster as Bumblebee alongside Frank Welker as Megatron and Soundwave and the late Peter Cullen as Optimus Prime. The short accompanies a 40th anniversary rerelease that exceeded initial box-office projections, prompting additional theatrical dates through Oct. 7. LeMaster said he initially underestimated the significance of the project because director Josh Wassung was a friend. FROM DISNEY MAGIC TO ANCIENT FAITH: DAVID HENRIE ON WHY GEN Z IS FLOCKING TO CHURCH "I thought this was my friend's little movie, this little Transformers movie that he was making for Hasbro," he said. Then he learned Cullen was involved. LeMaster praised the longtime Optimus Prime actor for embodying "strength and gentleness and kindness" and "protecting the weak." "Who am I? Why do I get to play Bumblebee?" LeMaster recalled wondering. For LeMaster, even the Transformers role connects back to his faith. "It's an opportunity to sort of spread good news in the kingdom through, you know, robots," he said. And despite joining the Autobots, LeMaster admitted Satan remains particularly fun to play. "I love playing the devil because he is so much like me," he said. "I know that sounds really weird." His Babylon Bee version of Satan is less fire-and-brimstone than frustrated corporate middle management. "What if the devil was an HR director?" LeMaster said. "You know, guys, it's been a rough quarter," he said in character. "Make sure that you put cover letters on all the things you turn in, please." Beneath the joke is a serious approach to portraying villains. LeMaster said he looks for something good in a character's motivations and then considers how it became distorted. "You always start with a good guy, and then you can twist it to something evil," LeMaster added. "That's kind of what I think the best villains end up being like."
